input.question: Is it possible that Mercury is the remnant core of a gas giant destroyed in a past supernova?
input.ground_truth: Any supernova close enough to rip mercury to shreds would have left a lot of evidence here on Earth which we do not see. We do have some subtle evidence of supernovae going off in the same neck of the woods as the sun some 10s of millions of years ago, but nothing that would impact the bulk properties of a planet nearby.

Some people wonder if Mercury, which is a small, rocky planet close to the Sun, is like that leftover center.

But scientists don't think so. They believe Mercury is just a little rocky planet that was left behind when the Solar System was made, not the leftover middle of a bigger, gassy planet that got blown up by a big space boom (called a supernova). The way Mercury is made and how the planets formed doesn't match what would be left after a big explosion like that.

So, it's a fun idea, but Mercury is probably just a little planet that stayed small, not a leftover piece from a giant cake that got smashed! 🍰✨
